data.title: Conserved Areas Explorer User Guide
data.summary: This guide introduces the CA Nature Conserved Areas Explorer and familiarizes users with key features and capabilities.

data.text: Introduction

The Conserved Areas Explorer is a series of dashboards that identify areas currently considered conserved for the 30x30 initiative using the California Protected Areas Database, U.S. Protected Areas Database, California Conservation Easement Database, and the California Marine Protected Areas networks.
Users can view information about how the lands and coastal waters are managed, and visualize what areas are currently conserved.
About the Explorer

data.alt: California 30x30 Logo

data.text: The CA Nature team developed the Conserved Areas Explorer as part of a suite of interactive mapping and visualization tools compiling statewide biodiversity, access, climate and conservation information to advance California's commitment to conserve 30 percent of our lands and coastal waters by 2030, known as the 30×30 initiative.
Learn More about CA Nature
This guide will help you learn:
• How the state defines conserved areas & data sources used
• The basics of how to use the Conserved Areas Explorer map viewer
• Using the Explorer's 'Detailed Terrestrial' and 'Detailed Marine' dashboards to delve into the data on conserved areas throughout the state
• Where to learn more about the state's 30x30 initiative & how to get involved
Exploring the Data
What is the definition of conserved areas for California's 30x30 goal?

30x30 Conservation Areas include land and coastal water areas that are durably protected and managed to sustain functional ecosystems, both intact and restored, and the diversity of life that they support.

data.alt: Background photo of Point Arena-Stornetta unit of the California Coastal National Monument by David Ledig, BLM, showing rugged rocky coastline in the foreground wrapping around misty ocean water with rocky islands and coastline visible in the distance.
data.attribution: Photo by David Ledig, BLM. Shared by BLM California.

data.text: Data Sources

The explorer draws its inventory of statewide protected lands from the California Protected Areas Database (CPAD), Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US), and the California Conservation Easements Database (CCED), which contain the most up to date information on public and private protected lands in California.

data.alt: Joshua tree forest against a blue, cloudy sky.
data.attribution: Credit Alessandra Puig-Santana, Natl. Park Service. Shared by Joshua Tree National Park on Flickr.

data.text: Classifying conservation status with GAP Codes

CPAD, PAD-US, and CCED classify an area's conservation status according to the United States Geological Survey’s Gap Analysis Project (GAP) codes, which assign a number 1 through 4 corresponding to the degree of protection a particular area receives.
A detailed description of GAP codes can be found here.
GAP Codes 1 & 2
GAP code 1 signifies the strongest protection measures on conserved lands.
GAP codes 1 and 2 are consistent with the state definition for 30x30 Conservation Areas and reflect an emphasis on biodiversity conservation.

data.alt:
Background photo showing the same image of Conway Summit Area of Critical Environmental Concern by Bob Wick, BLM, with an embedded table providing the following descriptions of GAP codes 1 and 2: 
“GAP Code Status 1 Description: An area having permanent protection from conversion of natural land cover and a mandated management plan in operation to maintain a natural state within which disturbance events (of natural type, frequency, intensity, and legacy) are allowed to proceed without interference or are mimicked through management.
GAP Code Status 2 Description: An area having permanent protection from conversion of natural land cover and a mandated management plan in operation to maintain a primarily natural state, but which may receive uses or management practices that degrade the quality of existing natural communities, including suppression of natural disturbance (for example, wildland fire or native insect outbreaks).”
data.attribution: Background photo by Bob Wick, BLM. Shared by BLM California.

data.text: GAP Codes 1
GAP code 1 signifies the strongest protection measures on conserved lands.
GAP Code 2
GAP Code 3
GAP 3 is mixed land-use with some biodiversity consideration, but insufficient to be categorized as 30x30 Conservation Areas.

data.alt:
Blurred background photo of Conway Summit Area of Critical Environmental Concern by Bob Wick, BLM, with an embedded table providing the following description of GAP code 3: 
“GAP Code Status 3 Description: An area having permanent protection from conversion of natural land cover for the majority of the area, but subject to extractive uses of either a broad, low intensity type (for example, logging, OHV recreation) or localized intense type (for example, mining). It also confers protection to federally listed endangered and threatened species throughout the area.”
data.attribution: Background photo by Bob Wick, BLM. Shared by BLM California.

data.text: GAP Code 4

GAP 4 indicates protections from intensive development; these areas may be conserved as open space– for use as agriculture, or local parks for instance– but have no known biodiversity management goals.

data.alt: “GAP Code Status 4 Description: There are no known public or private institutional mandates or legally recognized easements or deed restrictions held by the managing entity to prevent conversion of natural habitat types to anthropogenic habitat types. The area generally allows conversion to unnatural land cover throughout or management intent is unknown.”
data.attribution: Background photo by Bob Wick, BLM. Shared by BLM California.

data.text: Please note: The conserved areas data set contains areas whose conservation status could not be determined from immediately available data. Such areas may meet 30x30's textual definition but not currently be counted as 30x30 Conservation Areas.

If you have direct knowledge and supporting information about specific sites please use this link to initiate a review. The results of these reviews will inform updates to the CPAD, CCED, and PAD-US as appropriate for incorporation into future updates to CA Nature and tracking progress to 30x30.

data.text: Additional Datasets

The Explorer also draws on numerous other datasets representing designated boundaries for entities such as National Parks, Forests, and Monuments, Wild and Scenic Rivers, Wilderness Areas, State Marine Protection Areas, and National Marine Sanctuaries.

data.text: Overview Dashboard
The overview tab of the dashboard provides a summary of Terrestrial and Marine 30x30 Conservation Areas in California.

data.alt: Image showing the Overview dashboard tab of the Conserved Areas Explorer app.

data.text: Terrestrial 30x30 Conservation Areas
The left side of the dashboard highlights key statistics related to the statewide acreage of Terrestrial 30x30 Conservation Areas.

These Terrestrial Conservation Areas, shown in green on the map viewer, are comprised of lands assigned GAP codes 1 and 2 in the California Protected Areas Database (CPAD), the Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US), and the California Conservation Easements Database (CCED).
A detailed description of GAP codes can be found here.

data.alt: Animated GIF of the Overview dashboard with an embedded box first highlighting a pie chart of the state’s conserved terrestrial acreage and then highlighting the map viewer showing only the terrestrial conserved areas data layer.

data.text: Marine 30x30 Conservation Areas
The dashboard also highlights key information about the state's acreage of Marine 30x30 Conservation Areas, shown in blue on the map viewer.

Currently one type of marine managed area in California’s coastal waters clearly meets the definition for 30x30 Conservation Areas: California’s statewide network of 124 Marine Protected Areas (MPAs).
These areas include:

• State Marine Reserves (SMR)
  • State Marine Recreational Management Areas (SMRMA)
  • State Marine Conservation Areas (SMCA)
  • No-Take State Marine Conservation Areas (No-Take SMCA)
  • State Marine Parks (SMP)
  • Marine Life Refuges

data.alt: Animated GIF of the Overview dashboard with an embedded box first highlighting a pie chart of the state’s conserved marine acreage and then highlighting the map viewer showing only the marine conserved areas data layer.

data.text: Navigating the Overview Dashboard
The map on the right of the dashboard allows users to explore the state's current 30x30 terrestrial and marine conservation areas.
Controls in the top right corner of the map provide tools for enhanced navigation, including search, home, legend, and layers.

Tip: Navigate the map using your mouse, scrolling to zoom in and out, or alternatively utilize the plus and minus buttons in the bottom right of the map viewer. Pan to different areas of interest by clicking and dragging your mouse within the map.

data.alt: Image of the Explorer App overview dashboard with the search, home, legend, and layers buttons in the top right corner of the map viewer highlighted and identified with text and arrows embedded into the image.

data.text: Click the Search button and type in an address or location of interest into the search bar.
Results matching your search will appear in a drop-down menu. Select a result and the map will zoom to this location.
Tip: Click the Home button to return to the default view of all of California.

data.alt: Animated GIF of the Overview dashboard that shows the process of filtering the visible map to zoom in to view Yosemite National Park using the search tool, then using the home button to return to a view of the whole state.

data.text: ﻿The Legend button opens a pane that displays information about the visible data layers, including layer name and displayed color.
The Layers tool reveals the conserved areas and contextual data layers available in the map viewer.
Tip: Click on a layer name to view or hide a data layer.

data.alt: Animated GIF of the overview dashboard, showing the process of using the legend and layers navigation buttons to reveal and hide the map viewer legend, then reveal the list of map layers and click individual map layer names to reveal and hide the corresponding map data.

data.text: Click on any green terrestrial conservation area or a blue marine conservation area on the map to open a pop-up box with details about the conserved area.
Tip: Click Pan at the top of the pop-up box to center the map viewer on the selected conserved area; clicking Zoom to will take the map to a close-up view of the selected conserved area.

data.alt: Animated GIF of the Overview dashboard showing the cursor to first select a green conserved terrestrial area and then a blue conserved marine area from the Map viewer to open an informational pop-up about each of the selected areas, then using the ‘Pan’ and the ‘Zoom to’ buttons on the pop-up to center and zoom in on the selected marine area.

data.text: For greater context and additional capability to delve into the data on California's conserved areas, switch to the Detailed View at the top of the screen.

Tip: If you get lost along the way, additional high-level guidance on both the Overview and Detailed View dashboards can be accessed within the app by clicking the question mark next to each tab's name at the top of the screen.

data.alt:
Image of the Explorer App overview dashboard with an embedded arrow pointing to a small question mark at the top of the screen on the ‘Overview’ tab, which has been selected to reveal a pop-up window that contains the following text about the dashboard: 
“Overview Dashboard Information
To close this window click anywhere outside of it. 
•	30x30 sets California on the path to conserving 30% of California’s lands and coastal waters by 2030. This dashboard brings together conservation success stories from across the state, tallies their contributions towards 30x30 goals, and enables you to explore some of the data being used to track this progress.
•	The definition of conservation includes reference to the USGS’s GAP Codes. Gap Codes 1 and 2 are considered conserved, while 3 and 4 are not. For details on gap codes follow this link.
•	Conservation Categories 1 and 2 mirror the US Geological Survey's GAP definitions. GAP codes 1 and 2 reflect an emphasis on biodiversity conservation. GAP 3 is mixed land-use with some biodiversity consideration, but insufficient to be categorized as conserved. GAP 4 indicates protections from intensive development. GAP 4 areas may be conserved as open space, for use as agriculture, or local parks for instance, but have no known biodiversity management goals 
•	Click on the charts and map within the Overview dashboard that you’ll go to first to explore the currently conserved lands. 
•	In the bar chart, click on the GAP 1 column to update the dashboard to show how much of California has a GAP Code of 1 and where those locations are.”

Image of a landscape in the Cargo Muchacho Mountains, located east of the Imperial Sand Dunes, showing sand deposited amidst a reddish rocky landscape. In the background, dark mountains fade into fog against a light sky.
data.attribution: Credit Jesse Pluim, BLM. Shared by BLM California on Flickr.

data.text: Detailed Terrestrial Dashboard Tour
The Detailed Terrestrial View of the dashboard allows users to explore the state's conserved areas data with a much greater level of detail and context.
Customizable filters and interactive charts allow users to personalize their search and delve deeper into topics of interest.
Here you will learn about:

• Filtering app data by Conservation Status, Conservation Easements, and Geography;
  • Exploring data by various management agency levels and accessibility to the public, and;
  • Delving into the data based on different GAP conservation categories.

data.alt: Image showing the Detailed View dashboard tab of the Conserved Areas Explorer app.

data.text: Components of the Detailed View
The right side of the dashboard contains a map viewer displaying data on California's conserved areas with the same map navigation functions and capabilities as  the overview tab.
The leftmost panel of the Detailed dashboard contains filters which you can use to customize the geography and the type of data displayed.
The center of the dashboard contains several tiles with charts displaying key stats about the state's conserved areas.

Tip: When the conservation selection or any of the other filters are changed, the displayed map data and charts visible in the dashboard will automatically update to show customized information about the selected filter scenario.

data.alt: Animated GIF of the Detailed View dashboard with embedded boxes first highlighting the map viewer on the right side of the screen, then the filtering pane on the left side, then three tiles in the middle of the screen with charts displaying key statistics about state conserved areas, which will be further described in the following slides.

data.text: Filtering by Conservation Status Category
The leftmost panel of the Detailed dashboard contains filters which the user can use to customize their geography and the type of data displayed.

The default view of the app has the Conservation Selection filter set to display the State Definition of conserved areas, which includes only areas assigned GAP codes 1 and 2 in the California Protected Areas Database (CPAD) and the Conservation Easements Database (CCED).
Setting the filter to a Custom Selection will enable you to access and interact with areas assigned GAP codes 1 through 4.

data.alt: Animated GIF of Detailed dashboard showing the process of switching between the ‘State Definition’ and ‘Custom Selection’ Conservation Selection filter, which updates the dashboard to show information about areas with GAP Codes 1 through 4 when Custom Selection is selected then reverts to show only information about GAP Codes 1 and 2 when State Definition is selected.

data.text: Filtering by Conservation Easements
Users can further filter their search by conservation easements.

Selecting Easements Included will show the geography and associated data for owned lands drawn from the California Protected Areas Database (CPAD), as well as conserved areas in easements drawn from the California Conservation Easements Database (CCED).
If you select Easements Only, you will only see areas listed in the California Conservation Easements Database (CCED).

data.alt: Animated GIF of Detailed dashboard showing the process of switching between the ‘Easements Included’ and ‘Easements Only’ Conservation Easements filters, which updates the rest of the map based on this filter.

data.text: Filtering by Geography
Users can also filter to a certain geography by selecting either a specific County, a CA Climate Region, or 30x30 Ecoregion.

For example, if you select 'Klamath Mountains' in the Ecoregion filter menu, this will focus the map and the dashboard tile charts to only show information related to the conserved areas in this geography.

Tip: If a custom geography type is selected, users can toggle to the corresponding tab in the Conserved Area Acres tile to view a pie chart that captures information on conserved acreage for the filtered scenario.
If no corresponding tab is selected, this tile will continue show statewide summary information based on the other filters.

data.alt: Animated GIF of the Detailed dashboard that shows the process of filtering the visible map to zoom in to view Klamath Mountains Ecoregion using the Ecoregions filter, then selecting the Ecoregions tab in the Conserved Area Acres tile to view a pie chart about conserved areas in this Ecoregion.

data.text: Exploring Acres by GAP Conservation Category

In the Acres by GAP Conservation Category tile, you can click on the bar chart's GAP 1 data to update the dashboard to show the amount of California assigned a GAP Code of 1 and where those conserved areas are located.
Tip: To examine all Gap codes including GAP status 3 and 4, select the Custom Selection in the Conservation Selection filter.

data.alt: Animated GIF of Detailed dashboard showing the process of selecting GAP 1 data in the bar chart within the “Acres by GAP Conservation Category” tile to the dashboard by GAP conservation status, then switching to the “Custom Selection” Conservation Selection filter to reveal GAP codes 1 through 4.

data.text: Acres by Management Agency Level

The Management Agency Level tab at the bottom of the screen shows a breakdown of the types of agencies that manage the conserved areas you have filtered. Click on a bar within the chart to show the data for an individual management type.
Tip: If you navigate to the top right corner of a tile, a button will appear that allows you to expand that tile to the full extent of the dashboard viewer for enhanced exploration.

data.alt: Animated GIF of Detailed dashboard that shows the process of selecting a bar in the Acres by Management Agency Level tile chart to filter the dashboard by management agency type, then using the expand button in the top right corner of the tile to expand the map viewer to full screen.

data.text: Filtering by Access Type

Within the same tile displaying Acreage by Management Agency Level access type, users can navigate to a second tab at the bottom of the screen to show information about Accessibility of the conserved areas.

Tip: As with the other charts in the dashboard, you can delve deeper into the data by clicking on the Access category bar within the chart. Click the bar again to de-select and reset to all access categories.

data.alt: Animated GIF of Detailed dashboard that shows the process of selecting the “Access Type” tab at the bottom of the screen in the tile that, by default, shows “Acres by Management Agency Level,” then selecting the Access Type bar chart’s “Federal” data to filter the dashboard.

data.attribution: Credit David Ledig, BLM. Shared by BLM California on Flickr.

data.text: Detailed Marine Dashboard Tour

The Detailed Marine View of the dashboard allows users to delve into data on marine protected areas across California's coast and explore data by different protection categories, including state Marine Protected Areas (MPA) and National Marine Sanctuaries (NMS).
Here you will learn about:

• Which datasets are included in the detailed marine viewer;
  • Filtering the dashboard by protection category or viewing where those categories overlap, and;
  • Filtering the dashboard to examine a specific MPA.

data.alt: Image of the Detailed Marine Dashboard.

data.text: About the Data

The Detailed Marine viewer allows users to explore where California's coastal waters fall in State Marine Protected Areas, which currently meet the definition criteria for 30x30 Conservation Areas, as well as additional data on marine protection classifications, including areas in federally managed National Marine Sanctuaries

The Detailed Marine viewer allows users to explore where California's coastal waters fall into various protection categories, including state Marine Protected Areas (MPA) and areas in federally managed National Marine Sanctuaries (NMS).
California’s Marine Protected Areas meet the definition criteria for 30x30 Conservation Areas and are also shown in the Explorer's Overview Dashboard.

National Marine Sanctuaries partially meet the definition of 30x30 Conserved Areas. With strengthened protections, these areas could achieve durable conservation protections that move California towards its 30x30 goal for coastal waters, but they are not currently included as 30x30 Conserved Marine Areas
About the Data
California's coastal waters encompass a complex mosaic of overlapping marine managed areas that vary widely in purpose, level of protection, managing agency, and potential biodiversity benefits.
The Detailed Marine viewer allows users to explore data from two key data sources on marine managed areas:

• State Marine Protected Areas (SMAs), which currently meet the definition for 30x30 Conservation Areas. These areas are consistent with the 30x30 marine conservation areas shown in the Explorer's Overview Dashboard.

• National Marine Sanctuaries (NMS), which partially meet the definition of 30x30 Conserved Areas. With strengthened protections, these areas could achieve durable conservation protections that move California towards its 30x30 goal for coastal waters, but they are not currently included as 30x30 Conservation Areas.

data.alt: Image of the Detailed Marine Dashboard.

data.text: Filtering the Data
The filtering panel on the left side of the dashboard will allow you to delve into the various protection categories.
By default, the dashboard displays All State Marine Protected Areas (MPA), highlighted in blue.
Select All National Marine Sanctuaries (NMS) to switch to a map view of areas federally managed in an NMS.
Tip: Click an area of your displayed map to open an informational pop-up with details on the selected area

data.alt: Animated GIF of the Detailed Marine Dashboard showing the process of selecting the “All National Marine Sanctuaries (NMS)” filter to update the map, then selecting the “All State Marine Protected Areas (MPA) filter, zooming in on the map and clicking a mapped area to open an informational pop-up with details about the selected area.

data.text: Filtering the Data (continued)
Because California's coastal waters encompass a complex mosaic of overlapping marine managed areas, certain coastal waters fall into both an MPA and an NMS.
Select Overlapping MPA and NMS in the filtering pane to view areas included in datasets for both protection categories.
To view all the areas that are managed under at least one of the protection categories and potentially both, select Areas in either an MPA or NMS.
Tip: As you filter the map, the dashboard tile at the bottom of the screen will update to display key stats on protected acreage for the filtered data you have selected.

data.alt: Animated GIF of the Detailed Marine Dashboard showing the process of selecting the “Overlapping MPA and NMS” filter to update the map, then selecting the “Areas in either a MPA or NMS” filter.

data.text: Filtering MPAs by Name
To view a particular Marine Protected Area of interest, use the Search MPAs by name button in the filtering pane. You may type in the MPA's name or select one from the dropdown menu.
Tip: Click the 'layers' button from the top right corner of the map to add context data like Areas of Special Biological Significance, and view and hide visible map layers.

data.alt: Animated GIF of the Detailed Marine Dashboard showing the process of searching for a Marine Protected Area in the “Search MPA by name” menu, then using the ‘layers’ button in the top right corner of the map to view a list of layers and view and hide an additional context layer in the map viewer.

data.text: Explore a Spectrum of Conservation Approaches within 30x30

Meaningful conservation that contributes to California's 30x30 goal occurs in many forms across a broad spectrum of ecosystems, from strict protected areas, to working lands and waters. California’s vast array of landscapes all play important roles in biodiversity conservation, climate action, and access. Together, they create a mosaic of conserved areas working synergistically to support connectivity and redundancy—two key components of resilience.
To learn more about 30x30 and climate smart land management, visit our website at CaliforniaNature.ca.gov.
